coverage: First-round reference profile; identification and biographical details await review.

attestations.text: CHANG P'u 張溥 (T. 天如, H. 西銘), 1602–1641, founder of the politico-literary group known as Fu-shê 復社, was a native of T'ai-ts'ang, Kiangsu. An ardent student from youth up, he developed the habit of making frequent notes on what he had read, and therefore named his library, Ch'i-lu-chai 七錄齋, or "Seven-Recordings Studio".
